id_and_class.summary: Jiddu Krishnamurti held that ordinary consciousness is identical with its content, the conditioned deposit of memory, belief, fear, and self-image, and that the observer who seems to stand apart from experience is itself a product of thought. He proposed that choiceless awareness, observation without selecting, naming, or judging, can expose this division and end the inner conflict it sustains. In late dialogues with physicist David Bohm he also spoke of an unconditioned, universal mind, not produced by the brain, that can act through a quiet brain.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Its Conditioned Content; the Observer Is the Observed

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Ordinary consciousness is nothing over and above its content: beliefs, memories, fears, pleasures, and images laid down by thought. It is not a container, light, or witness in which contents appear.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Thought is the response of memory stored in brain cells, so Krishnamurti called thought matter and placed consciousness, in his sense, within matter. In the Bohm dialogues he separates this conditioned brain from a mind that is unconditioned and acts on the brain when it is quiet, though he posits no second substance.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not specified. Ordinary consciousness is a material process of memory, while the late ‘universal mind’ is said not to be produced by the brain, and Krishnamurti never reconciled the two in a formal ontology.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The self is not an owner of contents but is built from them. The apparent observer is assembled from the same memory as what it observes, so ‘the observer is the observed’: in anger, the controller who condemns the anger belongs to the same conditioned process.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Krishnamurti does not explain why physical processes have phenomenal character. He suggests that seeing and hearing can continue when the sense of a separate possessor recedes, which changes the organization of experience without blanking it.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Thought as material memory-process; psychological time as thought's construction; consciousness shared by all humanity; in late work, an unconditioned universal mind identified with intelligence and compassion, and a ground of stillness and energy from which order arises.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Direct observation in one's own experience. Krishnamurti rejected every system, method, and authority, his own included, and offered his statements as descriptions for listeners to test.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Content conditioned by culture and personal history; a thought-made division of observer and observed; psychological time sustaining the self's continuity. Beyond these lie choiceless awareness and insight.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-awareness and the sense of self; psychological conditioning; attention; transformation of experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Choiceless awareness: observation without an observer, in which the whole content of consciousness is seen at once and insight arises as immediate perception, not as a conclusion reached over time.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: When anger arises there is at first only anger; a moment later thought names it, recalls earlier anger, and posits an ‘I’ who has it. Effort and self-control presuppose this division and so maintain it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Content is shared across humanity: fear, sorrow, and desire are the same movement in everyone, which Krishnamurti compressed into the claim that one is the world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conditioned thought produces psychological conflict and dulls the brain. Krishnamurti claimed that insight, independent of the material process, can change brain cells and end conditioning, a claim Bohm noted lacked proof either way.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The accumulated image stands between perceiver and situation. Bohm later treated thought as a single system of conditioned reflexes that could gain a ‘proprioception’ of its own movement.
core_claims_and_evidence: The content of consciousness is consciousness, and the two are not separate.
The observer is a fragment of the observed that has taken itself to be separate, so effort to control oneself sustains inner conflict.
Thought, as the response of memory stored in the brain, is material and creates psychological time and the self's continuity.
Choiceless awareness and insight can end conditioning and, Krishnamurti claimed, renew brain cells.
In late dialogues with Bohm, the conditioned brain is distinguished from an unconditioned, universal mind that acts through a quiet brain.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: First-person contemplative observation, presented as findings of looking, not as hypotheses.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: None proposed. Contemporary work on nondual awareness (Josipovic and Miskovic, 2020) offers comparative vocabulary but not confirmation.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Iddo Landau challenges Krishnamurti's rejection of all spiritual methods, questioning the inference from an unconditioned goal to the uselessness of preparatory practice. His earlier description of brain, mind, and consciousness as one movement sits uneasily with the later talk of a mind separate from the brain. Similarity of human experiences does not establish that all people share one conscious subject.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether wholly unconditioned observation is possible, whether it transforms as claimed, and whether its phenomenology supports a universal mind all remain open. Krishnamurti does not explain qualia or say which organisms are conscious.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Strained. He treats consciousness as material yet affirms a mind not produced by the brain, and the strongest cosmological statements are Bohm's, to which Krishnamurti assents.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the personal self is assembled by thought from memory stored in the brain, nothing personal carries on. The universal mind of the late dialogues is impersonal.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: In the Bohm dialogues Krishnamurti tentatively assents that the universe is like the body of an absolute mind and that cosmic order is itself in meditation, with intelligence and compassion beyond memory.
